scope.execution: static analysis only; tests were not run

violations.description: The file-backed SQLite test always opens the same target/story-1-6-file-backed-test/ai-subscribe.sqlite3 path. Concurrent test processes or a previously interrupted run can share or lock that database, making the outcome depend on external filesystem state.
violations.suggestion: Create a per-test directory or filename using a scoped temporary-directory helper, process ID plus atomic sequence, and automatic cleanup; keep the independent in-memory SQLite tests unchanged.

determinism_evidence.random_sources: No Math.random, rand, or unseeded random source in the 22-file scope.
determinism_evidence.time_dependencies: No unmocked current-time assertion; demo timestamps are fixed fixtures and are not random.
determinism_evidence.ordering: SQLite catalog queries under test use explicit ORDER BY clauses.
determinism_evidence.concurrency: The 64-worker FFI test uses a Barrier and joins every handle; assertions depend on uniqueness/prefix rather than scheduling order.
determinism_evidence.temporary_paths: xtask sandboxes combine process ID and an atomic sequence and clean up on Drop; Windows credential targets use process ID plus atomic round. Only the file-backed demo SQLite case uses a cross-run fixed path.
determinism_evidence.external_calls: Browser tests replace Tauri/network behavior with deterministic fixtures and condition-based assertions.

recommendations: Give the file-backed demo database a unique scoped path per test process and remove it through automatic teardown.
Keep fixed demo values and explicit SQL ordering.
Retain Barrier plus join synchronization for concurrent correlation-ID assertions.
summary: The suite is strongly deterministic with one medium fixed-path race. Fixed demo values are intentional fixtures; OS time is not used for assertions, temporary test namespaces are otherwise process-scoped, and concurrent workers are explicitly synchronized.
